title: Marketplace listing — creative + ops checklist and launch notes
content:
Purpose:
This is the working checklist and creative brief for publishing Redwood Inference on cloud marketplaces (AWS/GCP/Azure + partner marketplaces). Focus: a pragmatic, ops-first checklist that pairs final copy snippets with required artifacts and owners so we can hand off the bundle to partner integration teams.

Status notes/to-self:
- Drafted after the alignment call on 2025-10-28.
- Still need final legal SKU strings and a confirmed meter plan from finance (MKTP-1123).
- UX screenshot set is partial (missing dedicated-console screens).
- Prioritize AWS first, then Azure, then GCP (region-fallthrough concerns).

Target marketplaces (primary order):
- AWS Marketplace (SaaS vendor listing + AMI image for private customers)
- Azure Marketplace (Managed App listing + partner offer)
- Google Cloud Marketplace (SaaS + container/Helm option)
- Select partner marketplaces (e.g., Snowflake Partner Connect) — lower priority, separate bundle

Audience / elevator copy (short, for listing header):
- One-liner (<= 140 chars): "Redwood Inference — predictable low-latency LLM inference with flexible deployment: hosted API, dedicated capacity, and VPC/private installs."
- 30–60 word summary (for marketplace teaser): "Deliver production-grade LLM inference across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. Redwood Inference combines a GPU-optimized serving runtime, smart routing, and observability tools so engineering teams can ship high-performance LLM features with predictable latency and cost."

Long description (marketing block, 2–3 paragraphs):
- Paragraph A: product framing (what it does, who for)
- Paragraph B: core differentiators (performance, unified API, fallbacks, cost controls)
- Paragraph C: deployment options + enterprise controls (SLA, VPC, KMS)

Feature bullets (short, scannable):
- Hosted API: REST/SDK, streaming, function/tool calling
- Dedicated: reserved GPU pools, autoscale, SLA-backed throughput
- Private: VPC/on-prem with KMS/HSM options and audit logs
- Optimize: batching/caching recommendations, quantization suggestions
- Console: per-route metrics, tracing, rollout controls

Benefits statements (for benefit tiles):
- Reduce per-token cost via intelligent caching and batching
- Keep apps online with automatic model fallback and routing policies
- Ship faster with a single API across environments

Technical/ops checklist (required artifacts and owners):
- Product copy and approved screenshots (Owner: Product Marketing — Priya)
  - Short headline (provided above)
  - Long description and feature bullets (finalized doc attached)
  - 3–5 screenshots: hosted-console-overview, dedicated-pool-dashboard, private-vpc-setup, latency-dashboard, billing-breakdown
  - One 60–90s demo video (optional but preferred)
- Legal & billing (Owner: Finance/Legal — Liam)
  - Billing SKU strings (final) and metering plan (per-token, per-embedding, optional reserved capacity)
  - Procurement docs: sample contract language for SOWs (BYOL/Private)
  - Export/compliance statements: data residency options, certifications summary
- Packaging & delivery (Owner: Solutions Eng — Diego)
  - SaaS offer definition (endpoint URLs, OAuth/OIDC flows)
  - Marketplace-specific artifacts: Azure offer package, AWS SaaS contract draft, GCP SaaS manifest
  - Container/AMI images (if required): repo links and version tags
  - Terraform/Helm examples for private deployments (repo link + docs)
- Security & compliance (Owner: Security — Jasper)
  - SOC2 status, ISO/other certs, pen test summary (attachments)
  - KMS/HSM integration instructions + key rotation notes
  - Network diagrams showing VPC peering and private-control-plane flows
- Billing/instrumentation (Owner: Eng-FinOps — TBD)
  - Usage reporting endpoint & sample payloads for the marketplace meter
  - Invoices and sample billing statements for reserved capacity commitments
- Integration tests & verification (Owner: Release Eng)
  - End-to-end smoke test runbook (list of tests and pass criteria)
  - Performance verification report for target SKUs (p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput)

Creative guidelines (do not stray from tone):
- Tone: concise, engineering-first, trust-building (avoid hype).
- Avoid "AI-first" buzzwords; prefer concrete verbs: "serve", "route", "cache", "pin".
- Use numbers where possible (e.g., "matches p99 latency targets for 128-token prompts").
- Keep the short description < 140 chars and the teaser < 60 words.

Assets checklist (files to attach to marketplace portal):
- logo: 512x512 PNG + transparent SVG
- banner: 1200x300 JP(E)G (or per marketplace spec)
- screenshots: PNGs 1920x1080 (annotated)
- demo video: mp4, 1080p, <= 90s
- whitepaper / one-pager PDF (product + deployment options)
- support contacts: email + escalation phone (CS playbook link)

Publishing workflow (high level steps + owner + ticket links):
1) Final copy + screenshots collected (Owner: PMM — Priya) — MKTP-1123
2) Legal signoff on SKU and contract language (Owner: Legal — Liam) — LEGAL-742
3) Build marketplace package and upload artifacts (Owner: Solutions Eng — Diego) — GIT#204
4) Run partner integration tests (Owner: Release Eng) — REL-330
5) Submit listing for partner review and respond to QA (Owner: Marketplace PM) — MKTP-1150
6) Approve listing + flip live (Owner: GTM Ops) — MKTP-1165

Launch comms playbook (minimal viable):
- Day 0: internal launch — enable docs, update pricing sheet, post in #announcements
- Day 1: Marketplace listing goes live — automated tweet + blog post (announce post draft attached)
- Day 7: Webinar/open office hours with Solutions Eng for partner onboarding

Support and SLAs: quick notes
- Default hosted SLA: 99.9% uptime (TBD, legal signoff required)
- Support tiers: standard (email + docs), premium (SLA, 24/7 escalation) — list support emails and on-call rotations in CS playbook

Metering and pricing model options (to discuss with Finance):
- Option A: usage metering (per-token generation + embeddings units) — aligns with hosted API pricing
- Option B: reserved monthly capacity (committed GPU hours) + overage rates
- Option C: flat monthly seat/license for private on-prem installs (with support tier)

Open questions / risk register (short):
- Who owns the AMI maintenance for AWS Marketplace images? (ops-level)
- Confirm whether Azure requires a managed app or a VM-based listing for our private bundle
- Metering schemas differ across marketplaces — map fields to our internal billing model
- Security certification documents may be out of date for some regions (need refresh)

Next steps & immediate TODOs:
- [Priya] finish screenshot set + write final long description (due 2025-11-12)
- [Liam] finalize SKU strings and contract blurb with Legal (due 2025-11-18)
- [Diego] build initial Azure offer package skeleton and push to GH (due 2025-11-20)
- [Jasper] attach latest SOC2 summary and pen test report to this doc (by 2025-11-12)

Notes for partner integrations (technical shorthand):
- We expose a single REST endpoint per region. Marketplace integration needs correct redirect URIs for OAuth (user-based auth flow for admin console) and an API-key provisioning flow for programmatic metering calls.
- For private offers, include installation script + postinstall hook to register with control plane (token exchange pattern).
- Telemetry: anonymized usage events are required by some marketplaces; have a toggle to opt-out for private/air-gapped installs.

Appendix / quick links:
- Confluence: MKTP marketplace reference (confluence:MKTP/marketplace-landing-v2)
- GH: infra/marketplace-integration (github:infra/marketplace-integration)
- Jira: MKTP-1123 (pricing/metering), MKTP-1150 (submission)

Rough meeting notes / brainstorm fragments:
- "Consider a lightweight free tier via marketplace to accelerate enterprise evals — but watch abuse/overage."
- "Could bundle Optimize as add-on SKU for cost-monitoring customers."
- "Ask platform team for automated latency snapshot generator for screenshot images."

End of doc — this is intentionally pragmatic and operational. Use as the single-source working checklist when packaging. Update linked tickets as things move.
